chunks: Muhammad, from Ahmad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Lays al-Muradi, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the slave woman, is her divorce allowed? He said: If she is your bondmaid, then no.
Indeed, Allah (Mighty and Majestic) says: 'A slave, the property of another, who has no power over anything.'
And if she is a bondmaid of other people, or a free woman, her divorce is allowed.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to divorce a slave woman in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a master cannot divorce his own slave wife because her legal autonomy is subsumed by his ownership, citing the Quranic archetype of the slave who 'has no power over anything.' This ruling distinguishes between the master-slave marital bond, which is unilateral, and the marriage of a slave owned by others or a free woman, which follows standard divorce procedures. This distinction highlights the nuanced interplay between property rights and personal status in early Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali: Muhammad, from Ahmad, from Ibn Fazzal Bin Salih, from Lays Al Murady who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the slave, is his divorce allowed?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If she was a bondmaid, so no.
Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is Saying [16:75] a slave, the property of another, (who) has no power over anything.
If she was a bondmaid of another people, or a free woman, his divorce is allowed’.
